question.worked_solution:
We proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to \infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{3}{\sqrt{{x}^{5}}}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{1}^{a}\frac{3}{\sqrt{{x}^{5}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{1}^{a}{x}^{-5/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{lim}_{a\to \infty }{[-\frac{2}{3}{x}^{-3/2}]}_{1}^{a} \\  & =-2\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{[\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{3}}}]}_{1}^{a} \\  & =-2\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{a}^{3}}}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{{1}^{3}}}) \\  & =-2(0-1) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
